alternative: Exception-based error contracts: define domain-specific StandardError subclasses and let raise/rescue carry the type, message, backtrace and cause; reserve dry-monads' Result/Success/Failure for code that is already written as an explicit monadic pipeline.
idiom_name: hand-rolled Success/Failure objects or dry-monads Result (not idiomatic in Ruby)
implementation_notes: Ruby's error channel is raise/rescue: an exception carries its class (the branchable reason), a message, a backtrace and a cause, and the language, the standard library and the ecosystem all assume it - dry-monads' Result monad is the only real Either-shaped option and it is a niche gem. Nothing in Ruby forces a caller to look at the failure branch either: with dynamic typing an unhandled branch silently yields nil, which is precisely the failure mode the pattern exists to prevent. Use Result-style values only where the code is deliberately written as a monadic pipeline (bind chains, do notation) and the team has agreed on the convention; everywhere else raise a domain error and rescue it where the policy lives.
code_sketch:
class PortError < StandardError; end

def parse_port(text)
  raise PortError, "not a number: #{text.inspect}" unless text.match?(/\A\d+\z/)

  port = Integer(text, 10)
  raise PortError, "port out of range: #{port}" unless (1..65_535).cover?(port)
  port
end

begin
  port = parse_port(raw)
rescue PortError => e
  warn "invalid: #{e.message}"     # class and message are the branchable reason
end
pitfalls: Two channels in one method: a raise inside code that otherwise returns Success/Failure forces callers to write both rescue and branch checks, and the branch check is always the one that gets forgotten.
An overly broad rescue StandardError swallows the NoMethodError or TypeError produced by a bug in the error handling itself, turning a crash into a silent wrong answer - rescue the specific classes.
dry-monads values are only as safe as the convention: Success/Failure can be ignored entirely, and unwrapping with value! raises Dry::Monads::UnwrapError, the Ruby-shaped unwrap().
Helpers that erase the reason (Integer(text) rescue nil, returning nil for 'not found') lose exactly what makes the failure branch actionable.
